A Note From Tim,

QUICK TIP

Box Breathing - Have you tried it? We’ve been doing breathing exercises after some of our yoga classes and Justin brought it back in during the Sunday HYROX Mobility and Yoga sessions. Where some breathing techniques are energizing, this is calming. 

Box breathing = equal-count inhale/hold/exhale/hold (often 4-4-4-4), used by Navy SEALs and elite athletes to regulate stress, improve concentration, and enhance endurance by slowing the heart rate down.

The benefits:
    •    Regulates heart rate and stress levels, helping people stay composed under pressure
    •    Calming, parasympathetic-activating effect — useful for anxiety in the moment, pre-performance nerves, or acute stress
    •    Deep breathing exercises like box breathing have been associated with improved mental clarity via increased blood flow

Got a stressful day? Wake up in the middle of the night and the mind starts racing? Headed into a big meeting?

Give it a try.
- Tim

Recipe Corner
This Week's Featured Recipe
High proteinPrep: 5 mincook: 15 minserves: 4
easy shrimp stir fry with mixed vegetables

Quick and easy shrimp and mixed vegetables stir fry with a homemade teriyaki sauce.

25g
Protein
332
calories
49g
Total carbs
6g
Fat
8g
Fiber
— 1 lb large shrimp (raw, deveined)
— 1 tsp sesame oil
— 800 g mixd frozen stir fry vegies
— 1/4 cup Lakanto golden monk fruit (at the Hub)
— 1/2 cup soy sauce
— 1 tbsp honey
— 2 tbsp rice vinegar
— 1 tsp groun ginger
— 1 clove of garlic (minced)
— 2 tsp corn startch (OR Xanthan gum for a keto replacement)
— 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
Instructions
1
Shake the corn starch (or xanthan gum) in a lidded container with 2 tsp of water to make a smooth mixture.
2
Put the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, golden monk fruit, honey, ginger, chopped garlic, cornstarch, and crushed red pepper flakes into a sauce pan and ix. Heat over medium heat, and stir often. The sauce should thicken in a few minutes.
3
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the mixed frozen vegetables and sauté until tender. Remove the teriyaki sauce from the heat when it's thickened.
4
Place the cooked vegetables aside in a covered bowl, and then heat the remaining olive oil in the pan. Peel the shrimp if needed, and then sauté them in the oil until just pink.
5
Add the vegetables back into the wok, and then add the homemade teriyaki sauce. Heat everything through, serve over rice or noodles and enjoy!
